concerns.analysis: The source document contains an agency logo ('NC Information Technology') on the first page, near the top left under the main title header. This is a meaningful organizational logo. However, the HTML output does not contain this logo, nor does the image manifest list any image matching its description. Since it is completely absent from the output, this constitutes a missing image defect.
concerns.source_pdf_quote: The 'NC Information Technology' logo located on page 1.
concerns.output_quote: The logo is completely missing from the HTML output.

concerns.description: Output has more images than source PDF (ratio 1.1x) — possible image duplication
concerns.analysis: image_count_ratio=1.08. More images in output than in source indicates duplicated or fabricated image elements.

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 18 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=18, examples=['https://krebsonsecurity.com/2017/03/why-i-always-tug-on-the-', 'https://ncconnect.sharepoint.com/sites/it_ext/esrmo_ext/Docu', 'http://it.nc.gov/statewide-resources/cybersecurity-and-risk-']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

On page 4, the source PDF contains footnotes where the document titles are underlined. In the extraction, these titles are pulled out as separate paragraphs but lose their underline formatting.

concerns.analysis: header_footer_count=2. Header/footer elements are present in extraction data. This is common in multi-page government PDFs and is typically cosmetic — the renderer strips them from HTML output.
